rationale:
Split into three children. All three are comparator-accepted declarations from other DAG branches, reused with their identical frozen Lean types. No new obligation and no new DAG node is created.

Why split. The supplied proof has seven steps. Two of them are general facts that are already proved, kernel-checked and accepted in the DAG, but are not in this node's frozen proof base:
- step 1, pairings with integer multiplicity triples: a.e. unit orientations, integrability, and |∫_{N₀∩E} φζ(β)| ≤ ‖β‖_∞·μ_R(K);
- step 4, a countable family of test forms that is C¹-uniformly dense with common compact supports (Simon's "countable dense set of ω", chapter-06.txt lines 1317–1322).
This node's Lean work may use only its comparator-approved children and the frozen proof base. Without the split, the formalizer would have to re-prove both facts; the second took three accepted nodes in the other branch (dor_lmbs_tfa_compact_exhaustion, dor_lmbs_tfa_covector_finiteDimensional, dor_lmbs_tfa_fixed_support_dense). Reuse makes the formal proof safer and avoids duplicate work. Since every child is already accepted, this node can start its Lean work immediately.

Children (supplied-proof step → child):
1. orient_bound = dpf_pfc_imrep_orient_abs_apply_le (node root.minimizing_implies_stationary-a1.diffeo_pushforward-a1.pushforward_current-a1.orient_bound-a1, commit 056f1b9b): step 1, first bullet.
2. pairing_bound = dpf_pfc_imrep_pairing_integrable_abs_le (node root.minimizing_implies_stationary-a1.diffeo_pushforward-a1.pushforward_current-a1.pairing_bound-a1, commit 5c8c6597): the rest of step 1. It uses it again with F = 1_E(β_k − β) and B = ‖β_k − β‖_∞, for the three estimates of step 6.
3. testform_dense = dor_lmbs_testForm_countable_approx (node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.limsup_mass_bound-a1.slicing-a1.testform_dense-a1, commit b7ecbda9): step 4, with U = ℝ^P.

What stays in the parent: steps 2, 3, 5, 6 and 7.
- Step 2: dominated convergence of the cut-offs γ_{t−ε,t}(f) → 1_{f<t}.
- Step 3: Lebesgue differentiation of s ↦ τ(R_s)(ω) on left intervals [t−ε, t], combined with hypothesis (ii).

No new child is proposed: a per-ω lemma for steps 2–3 would be used exactly once, and this node is at depth 5 of a depth-6 DAG, so such a child could not be split again. subproblems.title: IMRep orientations are a.e. unit: |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P and R = (M, θ, ξ) an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n). Then for Hⁿ⌞M-almost every x (i.e. μHE[n].restrict R.carrier-a.e.), every n-covector β ∈ Covector(ℝ^P, n) satisfies |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖, where ‖β‖ is the operator norm of β as a continuous alternating map.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[n].restrict R.carrier), ∀ β : Covector (Euclid P) n, |R.orient x β| ≤ ‖β‖
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse. This child is the comparator-accepted declaration dpf_pfc_imrep_orient_abs_apply_le (DAG node root.minimizing_implies_stationary-a1.diffeo_pushforward-a1.pushforward_current-a1.orient_bound-a1, status accepted, accepted candidate commit 056f1b9b0f63f29ad638c335a0b984ac1606c017). It is reused with its identical frozen type: the lean_statement below is string-identical to that node's frozen lean_statement, a whitespace-normalised comparison with the declaration theorem Submission.dpf_pfc_imrep_orient_abs_apply_le in commit 056f1b9b0f63f29ad638c335a0b984ac1606c017 matches exactly, and the type elaborates in the comparator's contract-mode challenge module after import GMT.Ch07.Submission. No new formalization is required; the accepted proof in that commit is the proof. Role in this node's proof: it is the first bullet of step 1 of the supplied proof (for H^k-a.e. x ∈ N₀, |ζ(x)(α)| ≤ ‖α‖, from the field orients), and the sibling pairing_bound uses it in its domination step 6. The accepted natural-language proof is reproduced below.

Source: Simon 6.3.1 (chapter-06.txt lines 735–746), as used in the first bullet of step 1 of the supplied proof of dtc_bc_lc_sl_slice_identity. In 6.3.1, for Hⁿ-a.e. x ∈ M, ξ(x) = τ₁ ∧ ⋯ ∧ τ_n for an orthonormal basis τ₁, …, τ_n of the approximate tangent space. The contract encodes this as IsUnitOrientationOf: ⟨α, ξ⟩ = ±α(τ₁, …, τ_n). Notation: μ := μHE[n].restrict R.carrier and ξ := R.orient. For an n-covector β (a continuous alternating map (ℝ^P)^n → ℝ), ‖β‖ is its operator norm.
1. Reduction to a pointwise claim. By the field R.orients, for μ-a.e. x there is a subspace Q of ℝ^P with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n R.carrier x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q. The a.e. filter is upward closed (filter_upwards). So it suffices to prove: if IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q holds for some Q, then |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖ for every n-covector β.
2. Unfolding the orientation. IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q provides an orthonormal τ : Fin n → ℝ^P (its span is Q, which is not needed) such that either
   (a) ξ(x)(α) = α(τ) for all n-covectors α, or
   (b) ξ(x)(α) = −α(τ) for all n-covectors α.
3. Operator-norm bound at τ. Let β be an n-covector.
   - The operator-norm inequality for continuous alternating maps (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm) gives ‖β(τ)‖ ≤ ‖β‖ · ∏_{i<n} ‖τ_i‖.
   - Orthonormality gives ‖τ_i‖ = 1 for every i, so the product is 1. For n = 0 it is the empty product, also 1.
   - Since β(τ) is real, ‖β(τ)‖ = |β(τ)|. Hence |β(τ)| ≤ ‖β‖.
4. Both signs. In case (a), |ξ(x)(β)| = |β(τ)| ≤ ‖β‖. In case (b), |ξ(x)(β)| = |−β(τ)| = |β(τ)| ≤ ‖β‖ (abs_neg).
5. Conclusion. For μ-a.e. x, every n-covector β satisfies |R.orient x β| ≤ ‖β‖, which is the claim.
proof_key_steps: Reuse the comparator-accepted declaration dpf_pfc_imrep_orient_abs_apply_le (commit 056f1b9b) with its identical frozen type; it is step 1, first bullet, of the supplied proof.
R.orients gives, μ-a.e., ξ(x) = ±(evaluation at an orthonormal τ).
Both signs give |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖; conclude by filter_upwards.

subproblems.title: Integrability and sup-norm estimate for the IMRep pairing with a bounded, compactly supported covector field
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, R = (M, θ, ξ) an IMRep U n, C ⊆ U compact and B ∈ ℝ. Let F : ℝ^P → Covector(ℝ^P, n) be a.e. strongly measurable for μ := Hⁿ⌞M (μHE[n].restrict R.carrier), with F(x) = 0 for all x ∉ C and ‖F(x)‖ ≤ B for all x. Then x ↦ θ(x)·ξ(x)(F(x)) is μ-integrable, and |∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(F(x)) dHⁿ(x)| ≤ B · (∫⁻_{M∩C} θ dHⁿ).toReal.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U C : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (F : Euclid P → Covector (Euclid P) n) (B : ℝ), IsCompact C → C ⊆ U → AEStronglyMeasurable F (μHE[n].restrict R.carrier) → (∀ x, x ∉ C → F x = 0) → (∀ x, ‖F x‖ ≤ B) → Integrable (fun x => (R.mult x : ℝ) * R.orient x (F x)) (μHE[n].restrict R.carrier) ∧ |∫ x in R.carrier, (R.mult x : ℝ) * R.orient x (F x) ∂μHE[n]| ≤ B * (∫⁻ x in R.carrier ∩ C, (R.mult x : ℝ≥0∞) ∂μHE[n]).toReal
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse. This child is the comparator-accepted declaration dpf_pfc_imrep_pairing_integrable_abs_le (DAG node root.minimizing_implies_stationary-a1.diffeo_pushforward-a1.pushforward_current-a1.pairing_bound-a1, status accepted, accepted candidate commit 5c8c6597411e77948b224fda014774beaa21ebaf). It is reused with its identical frozen type: the lean_statement below is string-identical to that node's frozen lean_statement, a whitespace-normalised comparison with the declaration theorem Submission.dpf_pfc_imrep_pairing_integrable_abs_le in commit 5c8c6597411e77948b224fda014774beaa21ebaf matches exactly, and the type elaborates in the comparator's contract-mode challenge module after import GMT.Ch07.Submission. No new formalization is required; the accepted proof in that commit is the proof. In the DAG that node depends exactly on the accepted node of the sibling orient_bound, so the dependency pairing_bound → orient_bound is recorded here as well. Role in this node's proof: it is step 1 of the supplied proof (integrability of φζ(β) on N₀ and |∫_{N₀∩E} φζ(β) dH^k| ≤ ‖β‖_∞·μ_R(K), where μ_R(K) = (∫⁻_{N₀∩K} φ dH^k).toReal < ∞). The parent uses it with U = ℝ^P and C = K compact, in two ways. (a) With F = β, a continuous field vanishing off K, bounded by B = sup‖β‖ (finite by compact support) and a.e. strongly measurable by continuity, it gives the integrability of x ↦ θ⟨dω, ξ⟩ on M and of x ↦ θ'⟨ω, ξ'⟩ on M'; these dominate the cut-off integrands in step 2. (b) With F = 1_E·(β_k − β), where E = {f < t} or E = ℝ^P is measurable because f is Borel, and B = sup‖β_k − β‖, it gives the three estimates of step 6. This uses the linear rewriting ∫_{N₀∩E} φζ(β_k) − ∫_{N₀∩E} φζ(β) = ∫_{N₀} φζ(1_E(β_k − β)) (integral_sub, setIntegral_indicator, linearity of ζ(x)). The accepted natural-language proof is reproduced below.

Source: step 1 of the supplied proof of dtc_bc_lc_sl_slice_identity (bounds for integer multiplicity triples). The accepted proof was written for Simon 6.2.24(2) (chapter-06.txt lines 414–425), where f_#T(ω) = ∫⟨ω(f(x)), df_x#ξ(x)⟩θ dHⁿ is said to make sense when M_W(T) < ∞ for W ⊂⊂ U; the printed text leaves the integrability and the estimate to the reader, and they are supplied here. This proof uses the sibling theorem orient_bound (Submission.dpf_pfc_imrep_orient_abs_apply_le).
Notation:
- M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, ξ := R.orient, μ := μHE[n].restrict M;
- h(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(F(x)), with θ(x) viewed in ℝ;
- 1_C θ := C.indicator (fun y => (θ y : ℝ)) and g(x) := B·(1_C θ)(x).
1. C is measurable. C is compact, hence closed (IsCompact.isClosed), hence a Borel, i.e. measurable, set.
2. θ is measurable. θ : ℝ^P → ℕ is measurable (R.measurable_mult), and every function on ℕ is measurable (measurable_from_nat). So x ↦ (θ(x) : ℝ) is measurable, hence a.e. strongly measurable.
3. Restriction identity. Since C is measurable, μ.restrict C = (μHE[n].restrict M).restrict C = μHE[n].restrict (C ∩ M) = μHE[n].restrict (M ∩ C) (Measure.restrict_restrict, inter_comm).
4. 1_C θ and g are μ-integrable.
   - By R.locallyIntegrable_mult applied to the compact set C ⊆ U, ∫⁻_{M∩C} θ dμHE[n] ≠ ∞.
   - Since θ(x) ≥ 0, its extended norm ‖(θ(x) : ℝ)‖ₑ equals (θ(x) : ℝ≥0∞) (Real.enorm_natCast). By step 3, ∫⁻ ‖θ‖ₑ d(μ.restrict C) = ∫⁻_{M∩C} θ dμHE[n] < ∞.
   - With step 2, θ is integrable on C with respect to μ (IntegrableOn).
   - Hence 1_C θ is μ-integrable (integrable_indicator_iff, C measurable), and so is g = B·1_C θ (Integrable.const_mul).
5. h is μ-a.e. strongly measurable.
   - The evaluation map (ζ, β) ↦ ζ(β) from MultiVector P n × Covector (Euclid P) n to ℝ is continuous, since ζ ranges over continuous linear maps (continuous_fst.clm_apply continuous_snd).
   - ξ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient), and so is F (hypothesis). So x ↦ ξ(x)(F(x)) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (Continuous.comp_aestronglyMeasurable₂).
   - Multiplying by the measurable θ of step 2 preserves this (AEStronglyMeasurable.mul).
6. Domination |h| ≤ g μ-a.e. By orient_bound, for μ-a.e. x, |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖ for all n-covectors β. Fix such an x.
   - If x ∈ C, then (1_C θ)(x) = θ(x). Using θ(x) ≥ 0 and ‖F(x)‖ ≤ B: |h(x)| = θ(x)·|ξ(x)(F(x))| ≤ θ(x)·‖F(x)‖ ≤ θ(x)·B = g(x).
   - If x ∉ C, then F(x) = 0 by hypothesis, so ξ(x)(F(x)) = 0 (ξ(x) is linear) and |h(x)| = 0. Also g(x) = B·0 = 0.
   Hence ‖h(x)‖ ≤ g(x) for μ-a.e. x.
7. Integrability. h is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (step 5) and dominated μ-a.e. by the μ-integrable g (steps 4 and 6). So h is μ-integrable (Integrable.mono'). This is the first conjunct.
8. Value of ∫ g dμ:
   ∫ g dμ = B·∫ 1_C θ dμ (integral_const_mul)
   = B·∫ θ d(μ.restrict C) (integral_indicator, C measurable)
   = B·∫ θ d(μHE[n].restrict (M ∩ C)) (step 3)
   = B·(∫⁻_{M∩C} ENNReal.ofReal(θ) dμHE[n]).toReal (integral_eq_lintegral_of_nonneg_ae; θ ≥ 0 and is a.e. strongly measurable)
   = B·(∫⁻_{M∩C} θ dμHE[n]).toReal (ENNReal.ofReal_natCast).
9. Estimate. By definition of the set integral, ∫_M θ ξ(F) dμHE[n] = ∫ h dμ. Then |∫ h dμ| = ‖∫ h dμ‖ ≤ ∫ g dμ (norm_integral_le_of_norm_le, using integrability of g and step 6). By step 8 this gives |∫_M θ ξ(F) dμHE[n]| ≤ B·(∫⁻_{M∩C} θ dμHE[n]).toReal, the second conjunct.
proof_key_steps: Reuse the comparator-accepted declaration dpf_pfc_imrep_pairing_integrable_abs_le (commit 5c8c6597) with its identical frozen type; it is step 1 of the supplied proof (integrability and |∫_{N₀∩E} φζ(β)| ≤ ‖β‖_∞ μ_R(K)).
C compact ⇒ measurable; θ measurable; μ.restrict C = Hⁿ⌞(M ∩ C).
Local integrability of θ on the compact C ⊆ U makes g = B·1_C θ μ-integrable.
h = θ·ξ(F) is a.e. strongly measurable via continuity of evaluation.
orient_bound together with F = 0 off C and ‖F‖ ≤ B gives |h| ≤ g μ-a.e.
Integrable.mono' gives integrability; |∫ h| ≤ ∫ g = B·(∫⁻_{M∩C} θ).toReal.

subproblems.title: A countable family of test forms that is C¹-sequentially dense in 𝒟ⁿ(U) with common compact supports
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open. Then there is a countable set D ⊆ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n: C^∞ compactly supported n-forms on ℝ^P whose topological support lies in U) with the following property. For every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) there are a compact set K ⊆ U with tsupport ω ⊆ K and a sequence (ω_k)_{k∈ℕ} in D such that tsupport ω_k ⊆ K for every k, ω_k → ω uniformly on ℝ^P, and dω_k → dω uniformly on ℝ^P. Here d = exteriorDerivative, and uniform convergence of covector-valued maps is with respect to the operator norm of covectors (the norm of Covector (Euclid P) k).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → ∃ D : Set (TestFormOn U n), D.Countable ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, ∃ (K : Set (Euclid P)) (ωs : ℕ → TestFormOn U n), IsCompact K ∧ K ⊆ U ∧ tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ K ∧ (∀ k, ωs k ∈ D) ∧ (∀ k, tsupport (ωs k : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ K) ∧ TendstoUniformly (fun k x => (ωs k : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) atTop ∧ TendstoUniformly (fun k x => exteriorDerivative (ωs k : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) (exteriorDerivative (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) atTop
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse. This child is the comparator-accepted declaration dor_lmbs_testForm_countable_approx (DAG node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.limsup_mass_bound-a1.slicing-a1.testform_dense-a1, status accepted, accepted candidate commit b7ecbda9150d7985c7094c40f6aebfb81c4ec24b). It is reused with its identical frozen type: the lean_statement below is string-identical to that node's frozen lean_statement, a whitespace-normalised comparison with the declaration theorem Submission.dor_lmbs_testForm_countable_approx in commit b7ecbda9150d7985c7094c40f6aebfb81c4ec24b matches exactly, and the type elaborates in the comparator's contract-mode challenge module after import GMT.Ch07.Submission. No new formalization is required; the accepted proof in that commit is the proof. Its accepted commit keeps the contract's import list unchanged. Role in this node's proof: it is step 4 of the supplied proof (Simon's "countable dense set of ω"), applied with U = ℝ^P (IsOpen univ; K ⊆ ℝ^P is automatic). For U = ℝ^P the exhaustion in step 1 below is K_i = closedBall(0, i), as in the supplied proof. It yields the countable family D of step 5. For each ω it also gives a compact K and forms ω_k ∈ D with tsupport ω_k ⊆ K, ω_k → ω and dω_k → dω uniformly on ℝ^P; step 6 uses these. The accepted natural-language proof, for an arbitrary open U, is reproduced below.

Source: step 4 of the supplied proof of dtc_bc_lc_sl_slice_identity ("a countable dense family of test forms"), which makes precise Simon's "by considering a countable dense set of ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U)" in the proof of Ch. 6, 4.5(2) (chapter-06.txt lines 1317–1322). Notation: Λ^k := Covector (ℝ^P) k with its operator norm, a finite-dimensional normed space; ‖η‖_∞ := sup_{x∈ℝ^P} ‖η(x)‖.

1. Exhaustion of U. If U = ∅, then 𝒟ⁿ(U) = {0} (tsupport ω ⊆ ∅ forces ω = 0), and D := {0}, K := ∅, ω_k := 0 work. Assume U ≠ ∅.
 - For i ≥ 1 let K_i := {x ∈ ℝ^P : |x| ≤ i and dist(x, ℝ^P ∖ U) ≥ 1/i}. If U = ℝ^P, read the distance condition as void, so K_i is the closed ball B̄_i(0).
 - K_i is closed and bounded, hence compact, and K_i ⊆ U.
 - K_i ⊆ int K_{i+1}: the open set {x : |x| < i + 1, dist(x, ℝ^P ∖ U) > 1/(i+1)} contains K_i and is contained in K_{i+1}.
 - ⋃_i K_i = U, because for x ∈ U, dist(x, ℝ^P ∖ U) > 0 (U is open).
 - Consequently every compact C ⊆ U lies in some K_i: the increasing open sets int K_{i+1} cover C, so finitely many do, hence one does.

2. The pieces X_i. Let X_i := {ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) : tsupport ω ⊆ K_i}. Each X_i contains 0.
 - For ω ∈ X_i, ω vanishes on the open set ℝ^P ∖ tsupport ω, so dω vanishes there too. Hence tsupport dω ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ K_i.
 - Equip X_i with the metric d_i(ω, η) := ‖ω − η‖_∞ + ‖dω − dη‖_∞. This is finite because ω − η and dω − dη are continuous and vanish off the compact K_i.

3. Isometric embedding into a separable space.
 - Let Y_i := C(K_i, Λⁿ) × C(K_i, Λ^{n+1}), with the metric given by the sum of the two uniform metrics. Since K_i is a compact metric space and Λⁿ, Λ^{n+1} are finite-dimensional, each C(K_i, Λ^k) is a separable metric space. In Mathlib: ContinuousMap.instSeparableSpace or ContinuousMap.instSecondCountableTopology for a compact second-countable domain, from Mathlib.Topology.ContinuousMap.SecondCountableSpace (the accepted formalization in commit b7ecbda9 needed no import change). On compact domains the compact-open topology coincides with uniform convergence. Hence Y_i is a separable metric space.
 - Define Φ_i : X_i → Y_i by Φ_i(ω) := (ω|_{K_i}, (dω)|_{K_i}).
 - For ω, η ∈ X_i, both ω − η and dω − dη vanish outside K_i, so their sup over ℝ^P equals their sup over K_i. Thus Φ_i is an isometry from (X_i, d_i) onto its image.

4. Countable dense subsets. Every subset of a separable metric space is separable. So Φ_i(X_i) has a countable dense subset, and pulling back along the isometry Φ_i gives a countable D_i ⊆ X_i with: for every ω ∈ X_i and every k ∈ ℕ there is η ∈ D_i with d_i(η, ω) < 1/(k+1).

5. The family D. Put D := ⋃_{i≥1} D_i. It is countable, as a countable union of countable sets, and D ⊆ 𝒟ⁿ(U).

6. Approximation. Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U).
 - ω is a test form, so tsupport ω is compact, and tsupport ω ⊆ U. By step 1, tsupport ω ⊆ K_i for some i, so ω ∈ X_i.
 - For each k choose ω_k ∈ D_i ⊆ D with d_i(ω_k, ω) < 1/(k+1) (step 4). Put K := K_i: it is compact, K ⊆ U, tsupport ω ⊆ K, and tsupport ω_k ⊆ K for all k.
 - Then ‖ω_k − ω‖_∞ < 1/(k+1) and ‖dω_k − dω‖_∞ < 1/(k+1). So ω_k → ω and dω_k → dω uniformly on ℝ^P; in Lean this is Metric.tendstoUniformly_iff, with dist = norm of the difference in Λ^k. ∎
